To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) state-based data breach laws have not prevented data breaches involving encrypted personal information and (2) state-based data breaches laws have not prevented unauthorized access to encrypted personal information.

1) the US state-based encryption safe harbours are not viable; 2) the US state legislatures have failed to consider the demanding practical requirements for the management of encryption; 3) the ALRC's proposal for a factor-based safe harbour may be a viable alternative to exemptions.

1) the viability of US state exemptions is questionable when examined in relation to breaches involving encrypted data; 2) the viability of the ALRC encryption safe harbour is also questionable; 3) the ALRC encryption factor is not sufficiently robust to provide a safe harbour from the notification requirement; and 4) the ALRC's encryption factor should be replaced with a more robust encryption safe harbour.
